paper_metadata.title: Effect of diffusion bonding parameters on the microstructure evolution of high Nb-TiAl and GH4169 alloy joints

evidence.quote: High Nb containing TiAl alloys are considered as potential high-temperature materials for low-pressure turbine blades.

mechanisms.name: residual stress relief by plastic deformation of thick diffusion layers

evidence.quote: at the elevated temperature of 950 ◦C, more sufficient atomic diffusion and thicker diffusion layers ( Fig. 9(c)) can promote stress relaxation through improved plastic accommodation capabilities and reduce the initiation and propagation of crack.

mechanisms.name: crack blunting by alternating columnar phases (τ3-Al3NiTi2 / α2-Ti3Al) in Layer-I

evidence.quote: the alternating arrangement of the columnar τ3-Al3NiTi2 phase and the α2-Ti3Al phase in diffusion Layer-I can effectively prevent crack propagation

mechanisms.name: vacancy/void formation by atomic diffusion acting as crack initiation sites

evidence.quote: Additionally, voids formed by atomic diffusion provide sites for crack initiation and propagation.

mechanisms.name: residual stress from thermophysical property mismatch

evidence.quote: the residual stresses arising from the thermophysical property mismatch between high Nb-TiAl alloy and GH4169 superalloy constitute another critical factor influencing the joint properties.
